target_customer: Solar asset owners, EPCs and O&M companies
problem: Inspecting and managing large solar farms manually is slow; O&M firms had drones but no software to analyze thermal imagery at scale.
business_model: B2B SaaS per MW/site for solar lifecycle management
product_category: Solar asset analytics and drone data software

founders.name: Nikhil Vadhavkar
founders.background_notes: Wrote thermal control simulations for NASA space suits; Gates Foundation drone grant.

founders.name: Eddie Obropta
education: BS 2013 and SM 2015 aeronautics and astronautics, MIT

technical_complexity.rationale: Thermal image analytics and ML on drone data; standard engineering with hard data-pipeline parts, built by MIT aerospace researchers.

defensibility.rationale: Processed about 4 GW of customer data by 2018 (MIT News), and data standards plus customer integration help, but others could build similar analytics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: In 2019 senseFly partnered with Raptor Maps for Solar 360 rather than building competing software; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: O&M firms were buying drones to replace manual solar inspections but lacked software (company blog); most 2017 users applied the software to solar farms (MIT News).

identity.logo: Raptor-themed name; no source reviewed on logo

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable name from drone roots; no source on brand pull. Name originated in agriculture drones, not solar.

pivots.why: Users applied the 2017 release mostly to solar farm thermal images (MIT News)

outcome_analysis: Raptor Maps won the MIT $100K in 2015, found agriculture was the wrong target, and moved fully to solar in early 2018 after users applied the software to solar farms. It raised $5M (2020), $22M (2022) and $35M (2024), grew to about 75 staff and 45 countries, and partnered with a drone maker rather than being copied. Pivot to a fast-growing market and customer data helped.
notes: Rounds from press; Series B and C investor lists from search summaries cross-checked by Mercom and company release. Name origin not found. YC participated in 2020 Series A; YC batch S16 per directory, MIT article does not mention YC. No competitor sources dated near 2016 were found (2026 vendor lists and a 2019 senseFly partnership are later). Low-quality aggregator pages ignored. Total raised not stated by company.
